chunks: Ali, from his father, from Ibn Abu Umeyr, from Ali Bin Yaqteen, from Abu Al-Hasan (peace be upon him), said:
I asked him about a man who went out on a journey, then staying (became apparent) for him while he was in his prayer. He said: He completes (the prayer) when staying becomes apparent for him.

key_terms.إِقَامَةٌ: Staying/Residency (specifically for ten days in fiqh)
key_terms.يُتِمُّ: He completes (referring to performing the full four-rak'ah prayer instead of the shortened two-rak'ah)

ai.seo_question: What should a traveler do with their prayer if they decide to stay in a place for ten days while already praying?
ai.summary: This hadith from al-Kafi clarifies the precise moment of transition for a traveler who decides to settle, ruling that the obligation to perform full prayer (tamm) begins immediately upon the emergence of the intention to stay, rather than waiting for the completion of the current prayer unit. This ruling underscores the Shia juristic principle that the state of travel is determined by the prevailing intention at the time of prayer, highlighting the flexibility within fiqh to accommodate changing circumstances during transit.
